findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed that the employee bathroom marked for “ladies” does not have a trash can with a lid. Ensure that all toilet rooms used by women have covered trash receptacles for disposal of hygiene products.
findings.citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
Observed there is an accumulation of mouse droppings in the dry storage area. There was also a young dead mouse on a sticky trap underneath dry storage shelving. The kitchen manager noticed the issue about a month ago, but it has gotten worse in the last two weeks. The inspector was informed that the issue is throughout the entire school. Pest control is performed by AAA Springfield Terminate every two weeks to a month. They are setting traps (i.e., buckets, sticky pads, spring traps), but the custodians are not aware of any spraying. They have having some success with trapping, particularly with young mice.

The following actions must be taken to eliminate pests:

- The dry storage area must be cleaned to remove the current droppings. Removing the droppings will allow the facility to better monitor the issue moving forward. They must communicate where they are seeing droppings appear with the pest control operator.
- The northeast corner of the dry storage room has the largest accumulation of droppings; including droppings on top of food storage containers. Upon the inspectors request, the kitchen manager removed all boxes from this area to allow better visibility. The ceiling tile above the corner also has what appears to be chew marks. The custodian present was notified about the potential entrance point and will be communicating with the pest control operator.
- The boxes in the dry storage area must be stored at least 6-inches above the ground. 
- Excess containers, food, and cardboard must be removed from the dry storage area. 
- Food throughout the kitchen must be kept closed to eliminate food sources; especially overnight. 
- The large holes underneath the dish machine must be sealed (ex. install a piece of plastic or metal over the holes). Additionally, seal any other holes (using steel wool) to prevent pests from entering the facility. 
- Communicate with the pest control operator about pest sightings and entrance points. Inspector suggests a more frequent schedule for visits. 

The kitchen manager had a conversation with Springfield School District 186 manager Megan McMillan during the inspection. They were also provided with SCDPH Environmental Health Director Colleen Kelly’s card for communication moving forward. An inspector will return in two weeks (1/30/2026) to check on progress to eliminate pests at the facility.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the shelving holding clean dishes surrounding the dish machine have an accumulation of dust. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the shelving is clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
There is a leak under the leftmost compartment of the 3 compartment sink. Repair the sink to eliminate the leak.
5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Caulking along the rear edge of the triple sink along the back wall next to the entrance to the dry storage area. The sink appears to have shifted pulling it away from the caulking. Re-caulk the sink and ensure that all surfaces subject to food and/or moisture are smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.
